name: Vector Tennis
tagline: 4,022 player-seasons of ATP and WTA behaviour, 16 masked features, and a ridge regression that beats "next year looks like this year" by +0.0941.
dims: 16 features x 4,022 player-seasons (2,035 WTA / 1,987 ATP). There is still no learned tennis tower — no embedding, no MTNN. The only model on this page is a ridge regression over the 16 masked feature columns.

headline_stats.label: gain in r over predicting next year's rank from this year's rank alone
matches across 28 fetched season files, 100.0% carrying a full ranking prior
sponsor tokens confirmed by both a venue rename and an equities name match

insights.title: Style adds 0.0941 on top of rank — and the raw r is not the story
insights.body: A ridge on this year's ranking column alone reproduces next year's ranking at r=0.7486. That is the persistence baseline: rank is sticky, and a page quoting the 16-feature model's r=0.8427 on its own would be selling persistence as if it were a model. The number that carries information is the gain, +0.0941. The split is temporal, not random — train on target year <= 2022 and test strictly after (2,032 train pairs, 894 test, 2,926 total) — because a random split puts the same player's adjacent years on opposite sides, and rank is persistent enough that the model would score well by memorising the player rather than learning anything, and would not match the actual use of predicting a season that has not happened. Sweeping the cut year across 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022 and 2023 leaves the gain positive at every cut, mean +0.0949, ranging from +0.0873 at the 2020 cut to +0.1059 at the 2021 cut. Shuffling the target collapses r to 0.0124.

insights.title: The sponsor was hiding in the tournament name
insights.body: The feasibility doc recorded the tennis sponsor rationale as failed at 0.29% coverage. That figure measured Wikidata P859, a sparse editorial property — a real value answering a different question. The sponsor of a tennis tournament is its name, and the name was already in the xlsx this repo had downloaded. Of 307 tournament-location pairs, 162 (52.8%) carry a candidate token, and 60 of 169 locations (35.5%) show a token arriving or departing at a fixed venue. Requiring both signals — the rename AND a match against 5,482 company-name tokens from the local equities universe — cuts 53 corroborated tokens to 36 confirmed. The strongest single piece of evidence is AEGON giving way to Viking at Birmingham and Eastbourne in the same year (AEGON present 2013-2018 at Birmingham, 2013-2017 at Eastbourne; Viking present 2021 at both). The file also names the false-positive class it refuses to hand-filter: Melbourne's 2021 quarantine-bubble events — Great Ocean Road, Murray River, Phillip Island, Yarra Valley — pass both tiers on Australian toponyms, because the stoplist only knows the one city in the location column.
insights.source: tennis_sponsors.json -> what_this_corrects, tournament_location_pairs, pairs_with_a_candidate_token/_pct, locations_with_a_rename/_pct, TIERS, equities_name_tokens, corroborated_count, CONFIRMED_count, CONFIRMED_strongest_evidence, CONFIRMED_detail.aegon / .viking, CONFIRMED_known_false_positive_class

insights.title: The k=6 clusters are quality tiers, and the file refuses to name them
insights.body: K-means was fit with the quality axis projected out, and quality still dominates what survived: PC1 takes 37.48% of variance against PC2's 10.36%, loading on WIN_RATE 0.41, DRAW_PROGRESS_MEAN 0.402 and GAMES_WON_PCT 0.397. Across the six clusters the largest spread on the quality columns is 2.631 (DRAW_PROGRESS_MEAN) against 2.225 on the behavioural ones (BIG_EVENT_SHARE). The verdict is quality tiering, not archetypes, and the file proposes no cluster names at all — labelling a k-means partition would launder it into a taxonomy. One cluster is exempted by the file's own stated rule (quality flat, a behavioural column past |z|=1.0): cluster 4, n=487, sits at max |z|=0.271 on quality with SURFACE_SPECIALISATION at +1.655.
insights.source: tennis_archetype_probe.json -> pc1_variance_share, pc2_variance_share, pc1_top_loadings, spread_across_clusters, max_spread_quality_cols, max_spread_behavioural_cols, verdict, naming_note, method_note, per_cluster['4'], role_like_clusters

insights.title: The ranking had to be lagged, and the corpus everyone used is gone
insights.body: An ATP or WTA ranking is computed from results, so correlating in-season rank against that season's win rate is close to correlating results with themselves. The probe lags the prior to the previous season's median rank, and the shrinkage confirms the contamination was real: ATP falls from 0.7527 same-season to 0.6088 lagged (shrinkage 0.191, n=1,253), WTA from 0.675 to 0.4962 (shrinkage 0.265, n=1,232). Both are still ruled usable. Closing odds were deliberately not used as the expectation — they are genuinely pre-match, but they are a near-optimal forecast of the very outcome being measured, so they belong as a baseline a model must beat. All of this runs on free per-season xlsx from tennis-data.co.uk, 28 of 28 seasons present, 67,080 of 67,081 rows with a full ranking prior and 99.9% with closing odds, robots disallow list respected. It runs there because the canonical free tennis corpus is no longer published: JeffSackmann/tennis_atp and tennis_wta 404 on both main and master, and the GitHub API reports public_repos=1 for that account, measured 2026-08-03.

game.prompt: Same season, same tour. Which player's ranking level came out better the FOLLOWING season?
game.axis_label: Next season's ENTERING_RANK_LOG (negated log rank — higher is better)

rounds.reveal: Both carried the same 2021 ranking level, -1.6094 (a rank of 5). In 2022 Kenin's level was -5.743 (312) over 17 matches for 4 wins; Sabalenka's was -1.9459 (7) over 55 matches for 33 wins.
In 2025 they were one step apart, Badosa at -2.4849 (12) and Rybakina at -2.3979 (11). In the partial 2026 file Badosa's level is -4.6396 (103.5) and Rybakina's is -1.0986 (3).

Thiem entered 2021 a step ahead at -1.6094 (5) to Tsitsipas's -1.7918 (6), but played only 16 matches that season. In 2022 Thiem's level was -5.2095 (183) over 34 matches; Tsitsipas held at -1.7918 (6) over 79 matches for 57 wins.
2016 had them close, Stephens at -3.2189 (25) and Wozniacki at -3.1355 (23). In 2017 Stephens's level was -5.0239 (152) over 23 matches; Wozniacki's was -2.4849 (12) over 82 matches for 60 wins.
In 2022 Isner was ahead at -3.2958 (27) to Rune's -3.4657 (32). In 2023 Isner's level was -4.5109 (91) over 23 matches for 9 wins; Rune's was -2.0794 (8) over 67 matches for 44 wins.
One step apart in 2022 — Pegula -2.4849 (12), Raducanu -2.5649 (13). In 2023 Pegula's level was -1.3863 (4) over 71 matches for 54 wins; Raducanu's was -4.3567 (78) over 10 matches.
Dimitrov held the better 2025 level, -2.8034 (16.5) to Auger-Aliassime's -3.1781 (24), off 30 matches to 73. In the partial 2026 file Auger-Aliassime is at -1.9459 (7) and Dimitrov at -4.9273 (138).
2023 had them near each other at -3.2387 (25.5) and -3.3844 (29.5). In 2024 Dimitrov's level was -2.3979 (11) over 63 matches for 45 wins; Shapovalov's was -4.804 (122) over 45 matches for 23 wins.

Barty led 2019 at -1.7918 (6) to Stephens's -2.1972 (9). In the shortened 2020 season Barty's level was -0.6931 (2) over 15 matches for 12 wins; Stephens's was -3.5835 (36) over 15 matches for 4 wins.

Djokovic's 2018 level was -2.5649 (13) — his lowest-ranked season in the file's ATP rows for him — against Kyrgios at -3.091 (22). In 2019 Djokovic was at -0.6931 (2) over 66 matches for 55 wins; Kyrgios at -3.6889 (40) over 35 matches for 21 wins.

caveat: No learned tennis tower exists — no embedding, no MTNN. The forward model is a ridge regression over 16 masked features, evaluated on a temporal split, and its value is the +0.0941 gain over the rank-only baseline rather than its raw r. The 16 features are behavioural only: the source carries no serve or shot statistics, so no style axis built on serving is derivable. The corpus is free per-season xlsx from tennis-data.co.uk, used because the canonical free tennis dataset (JeffSackmann/tennis_atp and tennis_wta) now 404s — measured 2026-08-03. The 2026 season file is partial (1,786 ATP and 1,731 WTA match rows against 2,644 and 2,505 for 2025). Sponsor tokens are name matches, not entity resolution: a token matching a company name does not prove that company sponsored that event.
